captions.caption: A black screen is shown.
The text "TORNADO TRACKERS" appears in white on a black screen.
A red triangular logo fades in above the text on the black screen.
The "TORNADO TRACKERS" logo is fully visible on a black screen.
A black screen is shown as background noise is heard.
A black screen is shown as background noise is heard.
A black screen is shown as background noise is heard.
A view of a grey, cloudy sky with a faint funnel cloud forming.
The funnel cloud becomes slightly more defined against the turbulent grey clouds.
The funnel cloud continues to form and descend from the cloud base.
The camera pans down, revealing the tornado's funnel extending towards the ground.
The view from inside a car shows the tornado funnel touching down in the distance.
The tornado is fully formed, seen over a rural landscape with a power pole.
The fully formed tornado is visible in the distance over a field.
The tornado spins in the distance, with a power line visible in the foreground.
The camera remains steady on the tornado over the rural landscape.
The view of the tornado continues, with the sky filled with grey clouds.
The camera zooms in slightly on the tornado.
The view of the tornado is steady as rain begins to obscure the scene.
Heavy rain and wind start to hit the vehicle, making the tornado harder to see.
The tornado is barely visible through the heavy rain and mist.
The view is mostly grey as the rain intensifies.
The view is partially blocked by the car's A-pillar, then shows a field.
The view is mostly grey and rainy, with the tornado out of frame.
The view shifts to show the silhouette of cows in a field.
Cows are seen in a field with large white tanks in the background, in rainy conditions.
The view pans across the field with cows, the sky is completely grey.
The camera pans left, showing more of the field and a power line.
The camera pans up to the grey, turbulent sky where the tornado was.
The sky is completely grey, with the tornado's form indistinct in the rain.
A power pole and lines are visible against the stormy grey sky.
The view is of the grey sky with little detail visible.
A new shot shows a wet rural road with a tree being battered by wind.
A tree on the side of the road is violently shaken by intense winds and rain.
The tree's branches are whipped back and forth by the storm's winds.
A swirling mass of rain and debris, the tornado, is visible behind the tree.
The tornado moves from left to right behind the violently shaking tree.
The camera pans right, following the tornado as it moves across the road.
Debris is seen flying through the air as the tornado crosses the road.
The view is momentarily obscured by a passing utility pole.
The camera pans back to the left, showing the tree still being battered by wind.
The tornado is now crossing the road directly in front of the camera's view.
A large amount of debris is visible swirling in the air as the tornado passes.
The tornado, a swirling mass of rain and debris, continues moving across the road.
The tree's branches are torn and tossed by the powerful winds.
The tornado moves further down the road, and a car's taillights are briefly visible.
The tree continues to be whipped by the wind as the main part of the tornado moves away.
The tree is severely bent by the strong winds from the tornado.
The camera remains focused on the tree being battered by the storm.
The wind continues to violently shake the tree on the side of the road.
The view cuts to a grey, rainy scene.
A new shot shows an oil pumpjack and tanks in a field through a rainy car window.
The view is blurry, framed by the interior of the car, looking at the tornado near the oil equipment.
The tornado is visible as a large, rain-wrapped column behind the oil pumpjack.
The camera tries to focus on the tornado, which is partially obscured by the car's interior.
A clearer view shows the rain-wrapped tornado moving behind the oil pumpjack.
The view is partially obscured by the car's A-pillar, with the tornado visible to the right.
The tornado is visible moving through the field behind the oil pumpjack.
The view of the tornado continues, with the oil pumpjack on the left.
The tornado moves further into the field, surrounded by rain and mist.
